body: Looks like a bug to me as `HttpContentEncoder` does add `Transfer-Encoding` header [here](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/HttpContentEncoder.java#L169) but `HttpContentDecoder` [does not](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/HttpContentDecoder.java#L101).
@NiteshKant agreed. want to submit a PR with a fix and unit test ?
@normanmaurer sure! I would be able to do this soon.
Sorry if I get it wrong, but why does `HttpContentDecompressor` remove the `Content-Length` header in the first place? `Content-Length` is the decompressed length, not the compressed one.
@slandelle I don't think so... Do you have a link to a the RFC that state this ?

issue.title: EOF for variable length, non chunked, compressed HTTP response is incorrectly treated as premature channel closure

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
The fundamental issue here (I think) is that HttpContentDecoder is modifying the incoming request headers to indicate the request is chunked when it might actually be variable length EOF terminated.

This happens here: https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/HttpContentDecoder.java#L102

This then causes https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/HttpObjectDecoder.java#L411 to yield a true value. The net effect of this is that a `PrematureChannelClosureException` is raised instead of emitting a `LastHttpContent`.

I wasn't able to create a test case for this because HttpContentEncoder enforces chunked responses. I discovered this issue when using Netty to reverse proxy a Jetty server, that uses EOF framing for streamed responses when not using keepalive.

I suspect that this is actually a regression caused by https://github.com/netty/netty/commit/ee0897a1d9d80119990964834d62f906f800afb8 as part of the fix for #5428.
